newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ capable of around 3 pct growth - Brash.
newsitem.headline: NZ capable of around 3 pct growth - Brash.

text.p: New Zealanders' expectations for economic growth were unrealistic, but the economy could grow as fast or faster than the U.K. and the United States, Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash said on Thursday.

Speaking at a lunchtime meeting of the Canterbury Employers' Chamber of Commerce, Brash said there was no evidence New Zealand could indefinitely support the very fast growth of five percent or six percent achieved in 1993 and 1994.

"What about New Zealanders' expectations for economic growth? Are these too quite unrealistic? I believe they are, at least based on current policies and attitudes," Brash said.He said the very fast growth of 1993 and 1994 was the result in part of one-off productivity gains from micro-economic reforms.
"If we want to build on that achievement in the years ahead, we must constantly be seeking areas where productivity can be further improved."
He said the bank based its economic projections on trend labour productivity growth of no more than 1.25 percent a year.
"If that turns out to be the case ... total growth in GDP could well be around three percent per annum because of growth in the labour force."
